title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 182 (Prohibitions and restrictions regarding political contributions)

content.overview: Section 182 allows a company, other than a Government company and a company which has been in existence for less than three financial years, to contribute any amount directly or indirectly to any political party. The contribution must be authorised by a resolution passed at a meeting of the Board of Directors, and the company must disclose the total amount contributed in its profit and loss account. The amount of contribution, and any prior statutory cap, must be checked against the text and amendments in force on the date of the contribution.
content.glance: Non-Government company in existence ≥3 financial years may contribute to a political party; Board resolution required; total disclosed in P&L; check current cap/amendments; Government companies and young companies barred.
content.study: A company, other than a Government company and a company which has been in existence for less than three financial years, may contribute any amount directly or indirectly to any political party. No contribution shall be made unless a resolution authorising the making of such contribution is passed at a meeting of the Board of Directors. The company shall disclose in its profit and loss account the total amount contributed by it under this section during the financial year to which the account relates. The expression “political party” means a political party registered under section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Current-law framing: confirm the company is not a Government company and has existed for at least three financial years; require Board resolution; check any statutory ceiling in force; ensure P&L disclosure. Foreign contribution questions fall under the foreign contribution law and are outside this section.

sections.heading: Eligible Company
sections.body: Any company other than a Government company and a company in existence for less than three financial years.

sections.heading: Board Authorisation
sections.body: Contribution requires a resolution passed at a meeting of the Board of Directors.

sections.heading: Disclosure
sections.body: Total amount contributed under the section during the financial year must be disclosed in the profit and loss account.

sections.heading: Cap and Amendments
sections.body: Any statutory ceiling or amendment in force on the date of contribution must be applied; do not rely on a repealed percentage without checking current text.

provisions.title: Prohibitions and restrictions regarding political contributions

examples.title: Young company barred
examples.body: A company incorporated eighteen months ago proposes a political contribution. Section 182 bars companies in existence for less than three financial years.

examples.title: Board resolution and disclosure
examples.body: An eligible company passes a Board resolution authorising a political contribution and discloses the total in its P&L. The formal requirements of s. 182 are met, subject to any ceiling in force.

hypotheticals.question: May a Government company contribute under s. 182?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 182 expressly excludes Government companies from the power to contribute to political parties.

distinctions.title: Political contributions (s. 182) vs charitable contributions (s. 181)
distinctions.left: Political parties; Board resolution; eligibility filters
distinctions.right: Bona fide charitable funds; 5% average-net-profits member gate

misconceptions.trap: Any company can make political contributions by ordinary Board action without checking existence period.
misconceptions.correction: Government companies and companies in existence for less than three financial years are barred. A Board resolution is mandatory.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 182 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm eligibility (not Government; ≥3 financial years). II. Require Board resolution. III. Check any ceiling in force. IV. Ensure P&L disclosure. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Eligibility facts; Board resolution; disclosure; precise relief.

examTips: Exclude Government companies and companies <3 financial years.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: State the eligibility and procedure for political contributions under s. 182.
Distinguish from charitable contributions and defence-fund contributions.
enhancement.definition: Section 182 permits eligible non-Government companies that have existed for at least three financial years to make political contributions authorised by Board resolution and disclosed in the P&L.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Corporate political funding is allowed only for established non-Government companies under Board control and public disclosure.
essentialIngredients: Disclosure of total in profit and loss account
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 182 is the political-contribution power with eligibility filters and transparency requirements.
enhancement.problemApplication: Test eligibility; require Board resolution; check disclosure and any ceiling.

verification.note: Section-text level; any percentage cap must be verified against amendments in force; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.
